newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul posts 718.7 bln won net surplus in 96 budget.
newsitem.headline: Seoul posts 718.7 bln won net surplus in 96 budget.

text.p: South Korea reported a 718.7 billion won net surplus in the 1996 state budget, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Monday.
The government collected 60.28 trillion won and spent 58.48 trillion won last year, making for a total budget surplus of 1.8 trillion won, a ministry statement said.
Of the surplus, 1.08 trillion won has already been accounted for in this year's state budget, it said.
How the remaining surplus amount will be used will be decided in June or July when the government draws up the supplementary budget for this year, a ministry official said.
In 1995, the government had a net budget surplus of 406.5 billion won and used the money as the base for last year's supplementary budget, he said.
Last year, tax revenues surpassed the budget by 44.71 billion won while spending fell short of the budget by 30.71 billion won. Non-tax revenues fell short by 35.5 billion won, the statement said.
The state budget for last year had been set at a balanced 60.11 trillion won including a supplementary budget. The budget for this year is set at a balanced 67.58 trillion won.
